elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Retained §5.1(a): IBM "will perform the Services using reasonable care and skill ... the degree of knowledge, skill and judgment customarily exercised by members of the applicable profession with respect to work of a similar nature" — a substantively equivalent professional-standard warranty.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "the software portions of the Base Components will conform in all material respects to their documentation".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Insert gives only "ninety (90) days following delivery" for the software conformance warranty, not twelve months.
Insert gives only "thirty (30) days following performance" for the Services conformance warranty.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Insert: "Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is repair, replacement or re-performance of the non-conforming Base Component or Services".
Insert: "or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Base Component or Services".

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in §5.1 as rendered; only care and skill, corporate authority, and the new conformance warranty.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code / virus warranty appears anywhere in the rendered §5.1 language.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Insert expressly warrants software to documentation: "for ninety (90) days following delivery, the software portions of the Base Components will conform in all material respects to their documentation" — an express software-to-documentation warranty at exactly the 90-day floor, placed inside §5.1 so §5.2's exclusivity clause preserves rather than displaces it.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Insert: "for thirty (30) days following performance, the Services will conform to the applicable Service Option Attachments" (Service Option Attachments is a defined term), meeting the 30-day floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Insert: remedy is "repair, replacement or re-performance of the non-conforming Base Component or Services".
Insert: "or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Base Component or Services".

reasons: Fallback level is complete: all four fallback elements (90-day software-to-documentation conformance, 30-day Services conformance, repair/replacement, refund) are met in operative inserted language, so the 'deviation' finding with a fallback-level redline is correctly positioned.

Preferred level fails on four elements: 12-month software period (only 90 days), 90-day Services period (only 30 days), compliance with applicable laws (absent), and no-malicious-code (absent). These are noted, not required, since the fallback checklist is complete.

Minimality holds: nothing existing was deleted or paraphrased, the insertion sits inside §5.1 rather than restructuring §5.2/§5.4, and it adds no survival tail, expense language, notice procedure or extra damages category. 're-performance' and 'in all material respects' track the playbook model language and the Services context, so they are not extras; 'in all material respects' is a Customer-side concession rather than an added requirement.

Intent preserved: no defined term is deleted, no cross-reference is broken, and the retained §5.2 exclusivity clause now captures the new warranty because it was drafted into §5.1. §5.4(a) (no uninterrupted/error-free operation, no obligation to correct all defects) coexists with a material-conformance standard.

Repair note (non-blocking): §5.4(c) still places "ALL MATERIALS AND ALL NON-IBM ... SOFTWARE" AS IS. If any software portions of the Base Components are non-IBM software, that retained sentence will be read to carve them out of the new warranty. Add "Except as expressly provided in Section 5.1," at the head of §5.4(c) (or limit the new warranty to IBM-provided software portions) to remove the overlap.

Drafting note (non-blocking): the inserted paragraph follows subsection b. without a subsection letter or connecting 'and'. Label it 'c.' and conform the 'and' at the end of b. so it plainly hangs off the §5.1 'IBM warrants that' chapeau.

Confirm 'Base Components' is a defined term in the Order Forms/Base Terms; if it is not defined in this agreement, replace it with the defined item (e.g., the software provided as part of the Services) to avoid an undefined trigger.
